Integration guide and endpoint reference

School ERP API for mobile apps

How a native Android, iOS, Flutter or React Native app talks to the School ERP backend: one subdomain per school, cookie sessions with CSRF protection, problem-details errors, and every endpoint with its fields, permissions and examples.

235 operations 359 schemas 75 error codes Generated 2026-10-23 from commit 91a72b1

Start here

The API is JSON over HTTPS under /api/v1/. It was built for the school's web app, and a mobile app uses it the same way: the same endpoints, the same cookie session, the same rules. There are no separate mobile endpoints and no API keys or bearer tokens.

Two kinds of people sign in. Parents use the parent portal endpoints to see their own children. Staff (teachers, office staff, accountants, principals) use the staff endpoints, and what each person may call depends on their role's permissions. One account can be both; GET /me returns areas: ["staff", "parent"] to tell you which experiences to offer.

The three rules a native client must follow
  1. Talk to the school's own subdomain (https://{school}.schoolerp.in) and keep a persistent cookie jar per app install.
  2. On every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, send X-CSRFToken (the csrftoken cookie's value) and an Origin header equal to the school's address.
  3. Read errors from the type and title of the problem body; title is written for end users and safe to show.

The machine-readable schema (openapi.json, OpenAPI 3.1) describes the same operations. Ask the team for it if you want to generate a client with openapi-generator (kotlin, swift5, dart-dio) or similar; every operation has a unique operationId, shown on each endpoint below.

Base URL and schools

Every school has its own subdomain, and the host name is the only thing that tells the server which school a request is for. There is no school-id header or parameter. All school data, sessions and cookies are kept per school.

EnvironmentSchool addressCookie names
Productionhttps://{school}.schoolerp.in
The final domain is still being set up; treat schoolerp.in as a placeholder and keep it configurable.		__Host-sid, __Host-csrftoken, __Host-did
Shared development serverhttp://northfield.100-88-158-51.sslip.io:8081
Reachable only on the team's private network. Ask for access and for demo logins.		sid, csrftoken, did
Local developmenthttp://northfield.schoolerp.localhost:8080sid, csrftoken, did

{school} is the school's short code (its slug), such as northfield: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Ask the user for it on first launch, or take it from a deep link or a QR code the school hands out. Then confirm it before showing the sign-in form:

  • GET /api/v1/school/branding returns the school's name, short name, logo and office email. Use it to show "Sign in to Northfield Public School".
  • A 404 with type …/school-not-found means the code is wrong, or the school is not active.

Because cookies are bound to the exact host, an app that serves several schools (a parent with children in two schools) needs no extra work: each school's cookies live under its own host in the same jar. Match cookie names by suffix (endsWith("csrftoken")) so the same code works in production and development.

Cookies and CSRF

Authentication is a server-side session identified by the sid cookie. Your HTTP client must keep and send cookies like a browser does. The cookies are:

CookieWhat it isReadable by the app
__Host-sidThe session. Set at sign-in, replaced at every sign-in, removed at sign-out.No (HttpOnly). Just store and send it.
__Host-csrftokenThe CSRF token. Set by GET /auth/csrf and replaced at sign-in.Yes. Copy its value into the X-CSRFToken header.
__Host-didA long-lived device id (400 days). Makes "trust this device" work and powers new-device sign-in alerts.No. Keep it across sign-outs so trusted devices stay trusted.

The __Host- prefix means each cookie is Secure, has Path=/ and no Domain, so it is sent only to the exact school host over HTTPS. Standard cookie stores (OkHttp with a cookie jar, HTTPCookieStorage, cookie_jar for Dart, the React Native native stack) handle this without changes.

What every unsafe request must carry

The server checks CSRF on every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, including public ones such as sign-in. Each of these requests needs:

  1. The cookiesYour cookie jar sends sid and csrftoken.
  2. X-CSRFToken: <value of the csrftoken cookie>Read the value from the jar right before each request. Don't cache it in memory: it changes at sign-in.
  3. Origin: https://northfield.schoolerp.inThe scheme and host (and the port, if it isn't the default) of the school address you are calling. Browsers add it automatically; native clients don't. Over HTTPS the server refuses an unsafe request that has neither Origin nor Referer.
The development servers won't catch a missing Origin Development runs over plain HTTP, where the server skips the Origin check when the header is absent. A client that forgets Origin works in development and fails in production with 403 csrf-failed. Send it from the first day.

Before the first unsafe request on a school (for example on the sign-in screen), call GET /api/v1/auth/csrf. It answers 204 and sets the csrftoken cookie. If an unsafe request ever answers 403 with type …/csrf-failed, call it again and retry the request once.

Web views and hybrid shells Requests made from inside a web view (Capacitor, Ionic, Cordova) come from an origin such as capacitor://localhost. The server sends no CORS headers, its cookies are SameSite=Lax, and the CSRF check rejects foreign origins, so those requests fail. Make API calls through the native HTTP layer (for Capacitor, CapacitorHttp) and set Origin to the school address as above.

Signing in

People sign in with an email address or a mobile number and a password. A number without a country code is read as Indian (9876543210 becomes +919876543210); full international numbers work too.

  1. Get the CSRF cookieGET /auth/csrf → 204.
  2. Send the passwordPOST /auth/login with {"identifier", "password", "remember": true}. The answer is {"status": …}:
    • signed_in: done. Read the new csrftoken cookie and go to step 4.
    • two_factor_required: the account has two-factor on. Go to step 3a.
    • two_factor_setup_required: the person's role requires two-factor and they haven't set it up. Go to step 3b.
    A wrong email, phone or password gives 400 invalid-credentials, always with the same message, whichever part was wrong.
  3. 3a · Enter the codePOST /auth/two-factor/verify with {"code", "trust_device"}. The code is the 6-digit number from the person's authenticator app, or one of their recovery codes. trust_device: true skips the code on this device for 30 days (it is tied to the did cookie). You have 10 minutes after the password; after that the answer is 401 session-expired and the person starts again from step 2. After 10 wrong codes the password is needed again.
  4. 3b · Set up two-factorPOST /auth/two-factor/setup returns secret_b32, otpauth_uri (show it as a QR code) and manual_key (for typing in). Then POST /auth/two-factor/setup/confirm with the first code returns {"status": "signed_in", "recovery_codes": [...]}. Show the recovery codes once and ask the person to save them; they can't be shown again. Both answers carry Cache-Control: no-store; don't log or cache them either.
  5. Load the personGET /me returns the user, their roles and permission codes, the school (with its timezone), the plan, two-factor state, session limits, display preferences, areas and upload_limit_mb. Call it after every sign-in and on every cold start; a 401 means the session is gone.
  6. Sign outPOST /auth/logout → 204. Then delete the sid and csrftoken cookies for that host (keep did). Sign-out works even when the school is suspended or read-only.

The whole exchange with curl

# 1. Get the CSRF cookie (the jar stores csrftoken)
curl -c jar.txt https://northfield.schoolerp.in/api/v1/auth/csrf

# 2. Sign in: cookie + X-CSRFToken + Origin
TOKEN=$(awk '$6 ~ /csrftoken$/ {print $7}' jar.txt)
curl -b jar.txt -c jar.txt https://northfield.schoolerp.in/api/v1/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-CSRFToken: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Origin: https://northfield.schoolerp.in" \
  -d '{"identifier": "9876543210", "password": "…", "remember": true}'
# → {"status": "signed_in"}, "two_factor_required" or "two_factor_setup_required"

# 3. The CSRF token changed at sign-in: read it again before the next POST
TOKEN=$(awk '$6 ~ /csrftoken$/ {print $7}' jar.txt)
curl -b jar.txt https://northfield.schoolerp.in/api/v1/me

Other public flows: password reset (always answers 202, whether or not an account matched; the link arrives by email) and invitations (staff and parents with an email get a link). Both links open the web app; if you add universal or app links later, the token endpoints are listed under Sign-in and session.

Parent activation slips

Many parents have no email address. The school office prints them an activation slip with a 10-character code (printed as XXXXX-XXXXX) tied to the parent's mobile number on file. A code works once, until 23:59 school time on the 14th day after it was printed. A parent app should offer "I have an activation slip" next to sign-in.

  1. Get the CSRF cookieGET /auth/csrf.
  2. Check phone and codePOST /auth/activation/verify with {"phone", "code"}. Case, spaces and the hyphen don't matter in the code. The answer is {"first_name", "school_name", "children": ["Aarav", …]}: show it so the parent knows they are in the right place. A wrong phone and a wrong code give the same 422 (on both fields), so nobody can learn which part was right. An expired or used code is a 422 on code ("Ask the school office for a new slip").
  3. Set a passwordWithin 15 minutes, POST /auth/activation/complete with {"password", "accept_policy": true}. The answer has the same status values as sign-in; continue exactly as in Signing in. After 15 minutes the answer is 401 activation-expired: start again from step 2.

From then on the parent signs in with their mobile number and the new password.

Session lifetimes

WhoIdle timeoutAbsolute limit
Parent-only account14 days without a request60 days after sign-in
Staff (anyone with a staff role, even if also a parent)Set by the school: GET /me → session.idle_timeout_minutes12 hours after sign-in
  • Any signed-in request resets the idle clock. GET /auth/session returns idle_expires_at and absolute_expires_at without resetting it, so you can show a countdown.
  • Staff should send "remember": true at sign-in. Without it the session cookie has no expiry date, and many cookie stores drop such cookies when the app is closed. Parents always get a 60-day cookie.
  • When a session ends, any request answers 401 with type …/not-authenticated or …/session-expired. Take the person to sign-in and keep what they were doing if you can.
  • People can see and end their sessions (GET /me/sessions) and their trusted devices. An admin can sign someone out everywhere. Expect a 401 at any time.

Data conventions

TopicRule
FormatJSON in UTF-8. Send Content-Type: application/json, except for the file uploads, which are multipart/form-data.
IDsUUID strings. They never change and are safe to store.
DatesYYYY-MM-DD, a calendar date in the school's timezone (attendance days, leave dates, birthdays). Don't convert them.
TimestampsISO 8601 with a UTC offset, such as 2026-10-23T04:30:00Z. Show them in the school's timezone from GET /me → school.timezone (usually Asia/Kolkata), not the phone's.
MoneyDecimal strings in rupees, such as "12500.00". Parse them with a decimal type (BigDecimal, Decimal); never use floating point. Show amounts in Indian grouping (₹1,25,000.00).
Partial updatesPATCH changes only the fields you send. An explicit null on a field that can't be empty is a 422 on that field.
Edit conflictsRecords with a version field expect you to send back the version you loaded. If someone saved in between, the answer is 409 edit-conflict with current_version; reload and let the person redo the change.
PaginationList endpoints that page take ?page=1&page_size=25 (page_size 1 to 100) and return {"count", "page", "page_size", "items": [...]}. A page past the end has no items; count is always the true total.
RetriesEndpoints marked Idempotency-Key accept that header: 1 to 64 letters, digits, - or _. Make a new key (a UUID) for each user action and send the same key when you retry it; a repeat returns the first result instead of creating a second record. Using a key for a different request is 422 idempotency-key-reused.
Request idsEvery response has an X-Request-ID header. You may send your own (a UUID) to match app logs with server logs. Include it in bug reports.
Academic yearsMany staff lists take ?year=<id> and default to the current academic year. A closed year is read-only (409 year-closed).

Errors

Every error is an RFC 9457 problem with Content-Type: application/problem+json. The machine-readable code is the last part of type; branch on that, not on title or the HTTP status alone. title is short, plain text for end users, so you can show it as is. Some problems add fields: errors (a list of {field, message}) on 422 validation-failed, retry_after on 429, current_version on 409 edit-conflict, and ref on 500 (quote it to support).

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Request-ID: 5f0c2a8e9b7d4c1fa3e6b2d8c4f1a9e7

{
  "type": "https://schoolerp.in/problems/validation-failed",
  "title": "Check the highlighted fields",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "",
  "errors": [
    {"field": "ends_on", "message": "The end date can't be before the start date"}
  ]
}

Field names in errors are the JSON keys you sent, with dots for nested fields. Show each message next to its field. When one request has several problems, all of them come back together.

Files and uploads

  • Uploads are multipart/form-data: student photos and the school logo (PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB), student documents (PDF, JPG or PNG up to 5 MB; the type is checked from the file's bytes, not its name), and the optional note on a parent's leave request. Spreadsheet imports may be larger, up to GET /me → upload_limit_mb.
  • Downloads: endpoints that end in /url or /document return a signed link to the file in storage, valid for 15 minutes. Ask for it when the person taps "Open", then fetch it straight away. The link needs no cookies; don't send the session cookie to it.
  • Images in responses (photo_url, logo_url) are also signed links that expire. Cache the image by the record's id, not by its URL, and refresh it from the latest response.
  • Viewing some files (documents, transfer certificates) is written to the school's audit log on every request, so fetch them only when the person asks.

A leave request from the parent app

POST /api/v1/portal/children/0b7e4f2a-…/leave-requests

X-CSRFToken: …
Origin: https://northfield.schoolerp.in
Idempotency-Key: 6f1d3c2e-8a4b-4f0e-9c7d-2b5a1e3f4d60

starts_on=2026-10-27
ends_on=2026-10-28
reason=Family function in Kochi
document=<optional PDF/JPG/PNG, up to 5 MB>

Notifications and push

  • In-app inbox: GET /notifications (paged), GET /notifications/unread-count for a badge, and endpoints to mark one or all as read.
  • Alert preferences: GET /me/alerts lists each category with its channels; PUT /me/alerts/{category} saves one.
  • Push today is Web Push only (/me/push/*, VAPID keys and browser push subscriptions). There is no Firebase Cloud Messaging or APNs channel yet. Until one is added, refresh the unread count when the app comes to the foreground. A native push channel is backend work; tell the team when you are ready to plan it.
  • When signing out on a device that registered for push, send its endpoint in the sign-out body ({"push_endpoint": "…"}) so that device stops getting the person's alerts.

Limits and school states

  • Attempt limits protect sign-in, two-factor codes, password reset and activation slips. Nobody is locked out; instead attempts that come too soon get 429 too-many-attempts with a Retry-After header (in seconds). Show the wait and disable the button until then.
  • Other endpoints have no published rate limit. Poll gently: once a minute at most, and only while the screen is visible.
  • School suspended: 403 school-suspended on every request except sign-out. Show a full-screen message; nothing else will work.
  • Maintenance: 423 school-read-only on writes; reads keep working. Ask the person to try again in a few minutes.
  • Plan limits: 403 not-in-plan for a feature the school's plan doesn't include, 409 plan-limit-reached when a count (such as students) is full.

Permissions and roles

Staff endpoints name the permission they need (shown on each endpoint below). GET /me → permissions lists the codes the person holds; use it to hide what they can't do, and still handle 403 permission-denied. A parent calling a staff endpoint gets 403 staff-only; a staff member with no linked child calling the portal gets 403 not-a-guardian. Roles that hold a permission marked 2FA must use two-factor, which is why their sign-in can answer two_factor_setup_required.

Client setup by platform

Each snippet keeps cookies across launches and adds Origin and X-CSRFToken to unsafe requests. Library names are the common choices for each platform; any cookie store with the same behaviour works.

// OkHttp: one client per app, a persistent cookie jar, CSRF + Origin on unsafe methods.
class CsrfInterceptor(private val jar: CookieJar) : Interceptor {
    override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
        val req = chain.request()
        if (req.method in setOf("GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS")) return chain.proceed(req)
        val origin = "${req.url.scheme}://${req.url.host}" +
            if (req.url.port != HttpUrl.defaultPort(req.url.scheme)) ":${req.url.port}" else ""
        val token = jar.loadForRequest(req.url).firstOrNull { it.name.endsWith("csrftoken") }?.value
        val builder = req.newBuilder().header("Origin", origin)
        if (token != null) builder.header("X-CSRFToken", token)
        return chain.proceed(builder.build())
    }
}
val jar = PersistentCookieJar(SetCookieCache(), SharedPrefsCookiePersistor(context))
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder().cookieJar(jar).addInterceptor(CsrfInterceptor(jar)).build()
// URLSession: the shared cookie storage persists across launches.
let config = URLSessionConfiguration.default
config.httpCookieStorage = HTTPCookieStorage.shared
config.httpCookieAcceptPolicy = .always
let session = URLSession(configuration: config)

func prepare(_ request: inout URLRequest) {
    guard let url = request.url, !["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"].contains(request.httpMethod ?? "GET")
    else { return }
    let port = url.port.map { ":\($0)" } ?? ""
    request.setValue("\(url.scheme!)://\(url.host!)\(port)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Origin")
    let token = HTTPCookieStorage.shared.cookies(for: url)?
        .first { $0.name.hasSuffix("csrftoken") }?.value
    if let token { request.setValue(token, forHTTPHeaderField: "X-CSRFToken") }
}
// Flutter: dio + dio_cookie_manager + cookie_jar (PersistCookieJar keeps session cookies too).
final jar = PersistCookieJar(storage: FileStorage('${appDir.path}/.cookies/'));
final dio = Dio(BaseOptions(baseUrl: 'https://northfield.schoolerp.in/api/v1'))
  ..interceptors.add(CookieManager(jar))
  ..interceptors.add(InterceptorsWrapper(onRequest: (options, handler) async {
    if (!['GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS'].contains(options.method)) {
      final uri = options.uri;
      final cookies = await jar.loadForRequest(uri);
      final csrf = cookies.where((c) => c.name.endsWith('csrftoken'));
      if (csrf.isNotEmpty) options.headers['X-CSRFToken'] = csrf.first.value;
      // hasPort is false for the scheme's default port, so this matches what the server expects
      options.headers['Origin'] = uri.hasPort
          ? '${uri.scheme}://${uri.host}:${uri.port}' : '${uri.scheme}://${uri.host}';
    }
    handler.next(options);
  }));
// React Native: fetch uses the platform cookie store;
// read the token with @react-native-cookies/cookies.
import CookieManager from '@react-native-cookies/cookies';

const ORIGIN = 'https://northfield.schoolerp.in';

export async function api(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
  const method = (init.method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase();
  const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
  if (!['GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS'].includes(method)) {
    const cookies = await CookieManager.get(ORIGIN);
    const name = Object.keys(cookies).find((n) => n.endsWith('csrftoken'));
    if (name) headers.set('X-CSRFToken', cookies[name].value);
    headers.set('Origin', ORIGIN);
  }
  return fetch(`${ORIGIN}/api/v1${path}`, { ...init, headers, credentials: 'include' });
}

Checklist before you ship

  • Sign-in, a POST after sign-in, and sign-out all work against an HTTPS server (not only the HTTP development one).
  • Cookies survive closing and reopening the app; a parent stays signed in for days.
  • A 401 anywhere takes the person to sign-in; a 403 csrf-failed refreshes the token and retries once.
  • Money is parsed as a decimal; dates are shown as sent and timestamps in the school's timezone.
  • Signed file links are requested on tap and never stored.
  • Leave requests send an Idempotency-Key, so a retry on a slow network doesn't file two requests.

Endpoint reference

Paths are shown without the /api/v1 prefix. Open an endpoint for its permission, headers, parameters, body fields and response examples. Examples are generated from the schema: the shapes are exact, the values are illustrations.
